chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
We found in the book of Ali (peace be upon him):
"Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah, and He bequeaths it to whom He wills of His servants; and the [good] end is for the righteous."
I and my family, who were bequeathed the earth, and we are the righteous, and the entire earth is for us.
So whoever revives a piece of land from among the Muslims, let him cultivate it and let him pay its land tax (kharaj) to the Imam from my family.
And he has what he consumed from it.
And if he left it and ruined it, and a man from the Muslims took it after him, cultivated it, and revived it, then he is more entitled to it than the one who left it.
Let him pay its land tax to the Imam from my family.
And he has what he consumed until the Rising One (al-Qa'im), peace be upon him, from my family appears with the sword.
He will gather it, prevent [others from taking it], and expel them from it, just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gathered it and prevented [others from taking it].
Except what was in the hands of our Shia, for he will grant them tenure over what was in their hands and leave the land in their hands."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on land ownership and tax payment to the Imam according to the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) citing a letter from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), establishes the ownership of the earth by the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt. It outlines the jurisprudence of land reclamation (ihya' al-mawat), stating that Muslims who revive dead land must pay the land tax (kharaj) to the Imam. The ruling remains in effect until the appearance of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), who will consolidate the land, expelling those who hold it, except for the Shia who will retain their tenure.
